doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Playing for Louis Armstrong as king of the Zulus and the Secret Nine
summary: De De recalls the brass band for Armstrong's Zulu parade and a baseball ceremony at the boys' home.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: You remember that book that I gave you that had your picture in it? It doesn't have your name underneath. On top, it's got a picture of Louie when he was king of the Zulus. And then underneath has a band, you know, the brass band. I don't know if you remember seeing that. That was the band I was in. I mean, is that time when the picture was taken? Yeah, that's Cuckoo and George Lewis.
Didn't you play for Louie when he was king of the Zulus? Yeah, yeah, yeah.
I played, uh, when the floor broke down. Yeah, I was playing then, yeah. And we had the same band.
Whose band was that? George Lewis's or what? No.

That was a book. Glass. Henry Glass. It was his band. Oh, I see. And then, no, John Cashmere. Cashmere. John Cashmere. He's a pioneer in that place. It was his band. Oh, I don't understand. He's a pioneer in that place. I played for Lewis during the time, uh, he threw the first ball at, uh, boys home, LaFont's home. LaFont's home. He gave me the trippy on. He gave him the outfit, the boys, uh, suit the boys home. He gave him their baseball suits. And I played, uh, played the dance afterwards, you know. Played for the game. I presented him with the suits. And the whole outfit, the gloves, bats, and all that, and all that stuff. And he threw the first ball out, you know. It opened the game. What is it?
I think that's what he called the balls.
I believe it was at the time. I believe it was. LaFont's home. Because he was in the home, you know. Yeah. Yeah. And Rene, too. You know, kid. Rene, also.
Yeah. Big boys at the time.
